info.title: Rustrak
info.description: Ultra-lightweight error tracking server compatible with Sentry SDKs

get.summary: GET /api/0/issues/{issue_id}/
get.description:
One issue with its releases and its 24h and 30d series (Sentry's
`GroupDetailsEndpoint`). Also served under `/groups/` and the
organization-scoped paths, as Sentry does.

put.description:
Sets an issue's status and returns the issue (Sentry's
`GroupDetailsEndpoint.put`). The change goes through Rustrak's own
issue update, so it is recorded and mirrored like any other.

post.summary: Assemble uploaded chunks into debug information files (ProGuard mappings, JVM source bundles).
post.description:
Sentry's `DifAssembleEndpoint`: the body maps each file's SHA-1 to its
name, chunks and optional debug ID, and the answer maps it to its state.

200.description: Assembly state per file checksum (not_found / created / assembling / ok / error)

post.summary: Upload a zip of debug information files (the path `sentry-cli upload-proguard` takes).
post.description:
Sentry's `DebugFilesEndpoint.post` processes the zip in the request.
Here each file goes through the assembly worker instead, the same as a
chunked upload, because building a ProGuard cache can take gigabytes.
Only ProGuard mappings are recognised; other entries are skipped.

requestBody.description: A `file` part: a zip of debug files, such as `proguard/<uuid>.txt`

201.description: The debug files queued for processing

post.summary: POST /api/0/projects/{org_slug}/{project_slug}/releases/
post.description:
Sentry-compatible release creation. Idempotent: repeating the same
`(project, version)` returns 208 rather than erroring — sentry-cli and JS
bundler plugins call this on every build. Triggers date-based regression
clearing (see [`crate::services::issue::IssueService::finalize_release`])
on every call, not just the new-row branch: `finalize_release`'s own
`UPDATE ... WHERE` is idempotent (a repeat run affects 0 rows once nothing
is left to clear), so this also self-heals a prior call that created the
row but failed before clearing ran — a plain `if created` gate would
otherwise skip clearing forever once a retry lands on the 208 branch.

208.description: Release already exists — no duplicate created

put.description:
Generic partial update (`ref`, `url`, `dateReleased`). Setting
`dateReleased` IS "finalize" — there is no separate status flag.

post.summary: POST /api/0/projects/{org_slug}/{project_slug}/user-feedback/
post.description:
Submit a user report about an error event (Sentry's
`ProjectUserReportsEndpoint`, `feedback/endpoints/project_user_reports.py`).
Accepts `Authorization: DSN <dsn>` as well as a token; the report becomes a
feedback, as the `user_report` envelope item does.

200.description: The report, or an empty body under DSN auth

get.summary: GET /api/projects - List projects with pagination
get.description: Admins see every project. Non-admins see only the projects they belong to.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order direction (default: desc = newest first)

parameters.name: stats_period
parameters.description:
Window for the per-project stats on each row (e.g. `24h`, `7d`).

Omitted means the caller does not want stats at all, and the extra
aggregate queries are skipped entirely — this is what keeps the plain
`GET /api/projects` that SDK tooling and the project picker use as
cheap as it was before the list table grew a sparkline. Sentry's own
projects endpoint gates its `stats` field on `?statsPeriod=` the same
way.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: The project's own limits, or `null` when it follows the operator's.

rate_limited_event_count.description: Events the quota dropped after ingest had accepted them.

sentry_key.description:
The DSN's public key: its 32 hex digits in hyphenated UUID form
(8-4-4-4-12), not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID. The DSN carries the
same key without hyphens.

oneOf.description:
Present only when the request asked for `?stats_period=`.

Absent rather than zeroed when unrequested: a caller that did not ask
must be able to tell "no stats were computed" from "this project is
quiet", and only one of those should render an empty sparkline.

get.summary:
GET /api/projects/{project_id}/agents/traces
Paginated per-trace_id aggregate (duration, tokens, tool usage) across
all AI spans sharing that trace, regardless of origin.

parameters.name: period_hours
parameters.description:
Lookback window in hours (default: all time, no filter). The dashboard
applies one window to every widget, and this table is one of them.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: Restrict to spans reporting this environment (default: all).

items.description:
One row of the Traces table — per-`trace_id` aggregate across all AI
spans (standalone and transaction-embedded) sharing that trace.

agent_names.description:
Every distinct agent that ran in this trace, earliest first. A trace
with handoffs involves more than one, so this is a list rather than a
single root name — Sentry's own Traces table shows them all.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the root/longest AI span in this trace, in milliseconds.

error_count.description: AI spans in this trace whose status is set and not `ok`.

llm_call_count.description:
`ai_client` spans in this trace — how many times a model was actually
called, which is what separates a one-shot answer from an agent loop.

GET /api/projects/{project_id}/spans
Lists spans for a project with offset-based pagination (newest by
start_timestamp first), optionally filtered by op/status/trace_id.
Returns spans regardless of origin — standalone or extracted from a
transaction — since both are stored in the same table.

parameters.name: trace_id
parameters.description:
Filter by trace id — matches spans regardless of origin (standalone
or extracted from a transaction), since both share this table.

items.description:
A single indexed span — extracted from a transaction, OR standalone
(Sentry "span" item type). Both origins write into the same `spans`
table, so `transaction_id` is the only thing that distinguishes them.

exclusive_time_ms.description: Relay's exclusive (self) time in milliseconds, if provided by the SDK.

gen_ai_operation_type.description:
gen_ai.* denormalized fields (story-ai-agent-monitoring.md, GH #180).
All `None` unless the span was recognized as an AI span.

platform.description:
Set for every span. A standalone span reports its own; a
transaction-embedded one is stamped with its parent transaction's at
write time, rather than being left NULL to be recovered by a JOIN —
the agents dashboard filters `spans` directly and a NULL would drop
the row from an environment-filtered view.

transaction_id.description:
The parent transaction, if this span was extracted from one.
`None` for a standalone span.

parameters.name: span_id
parameters.description: Span row ID (the `id` field of a span list item, not the SDK's 16-hex span_id)

200.description: Span with its full attribute bag

get.summary: GET /api/storage/projects — per-project counts and estimated weight.

items.description:

Counts are exact. `estimated_bytes` estimates the JSON payload length this
project holds across events, transactions, spans and logs: a sample of its
newest rows per table (spans, which have no ingest time, are sampled in no
particular order), scaled by the row count. It is exact for a project with
no more rows than the sample.

Requires a session cookie or a Bearer token, unlike its neighbours in this
scope. `/health` and `/health/ready` answer "is this process up", which a
probe has to be able to ask without credentials; this one answers "which
build is this", which is the first thing worth knowing about a host you
intend to attack.

get.summary: GET /{org_slug}/{project_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/
get.description:
The issue page GitLab's "View in Sentry" opens: Sentry redirects this
legacy path to the issue (`static/app/router/routes.tsx`), Rustrak to its
dashboard. A visitor who is not signed in goes to the login page instead,
so a stranger learns nothing about which issues exist.

parameters.name: project_slug
parameters.description: Project slug (ignored: the id names the issue)

302.description: Browser redirect to the issue in the dashboard, or to the login page

signed_in.description:
Whether the response opened a session. False when password login is
disabled: the account exists, and its owner signs in through SSO.

ActivityEntry.description:
An entry in an issue's activity log. Comments are stored as activity rows of
type `note` with `{"text": ...}` in `data` (Sentry models notes as activity).

AgentDurationPoint.description: avg/p95 duration for one time bucket.

AgentModelRow.description:
One row of the Models table: per response model, the volume, the failures,
the latency and the full token split.

Cached input and reasoning output are SUBSETS of input/output, not
additions — a reader comparing them must not add all four together.

AgentSummary.description:
Headline numbers for the agents dashboard, over the selected window.

Token totals exclude `agent`-type spans throughout, for the same reason
the Traces table does: an agent span's usage is a client-side rollup of
its `ai_client` children, so counting both double-counts.

avg_duration_ms.description: Over `agent` and `ai_client` spans — matching the Duration chart.

error_count.description: AI spans whose status is set and not `ok`.

AgentTimeseriesPoint.description: One time-bucketed value (count or sum) — mirrors `SessionTimeseriesPoint`.

AgentToolRow.description:
One row of the Tools table: per tool, how often it ran and how often it
failed. A tool with a high failure rate is the most actionable signal the
agents page can carry.

AgentTraceSummary.description:
One row of the Traces table — per-`trace_id` aggregate across all AI
spans (standalone and transaction-embedded) sharing that trace.

agent_names.description:
Every distinct agent that ran in this trace, earliest first. A trace
with handoffs involves more than one, so this is a list rather than a
single root name — Sentry's own Traces table shows them all.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the root/longest AI span in this trace, in milliseconds.

error_count.description: AI spans in this trace whose status is set and not `ok`.

llm_call_count.description:
`ai_client` spans in this trace — how many times a model was actually
called, which is what separates a one-shot answer from an agent loop.

AlertHistory.description: Alert delivery history record (audit log and retry queue)

AlertIntegration.description: Global alert integration record — stores credentials only, no routing.

AlertRuleChannelInput.description: DTO for a channel with routing override in rule create/update

AlertRuleResponse.description: Response for alert rule including linked integration info

channels.description: All linked integrations including routing_override per channel.

integration_ids.description: Flat list of integration IDs (backward compat, derived from channels).

AlertStatus.description: Status of an alert delivery attempt

AttachmentBytes.description:
The raw bytes of an attachment. Untyped in the spec: the generated
client validates bodies with zod, which has no type for a binary one.

content_type.description: As the SDK declared it; the download trusts only the bytes.

event_id.description: The event it was sent with (the stored row's id).

AuthTokenCreatedResponse.description: Response that includes the full token (only on creation)

AuthorizationDecision.description: The user's answer to a consent screen.

AuthorizationInfo.description: What the consent page shows about the client asking.

redirect_host.description: Host the user is sent back to, the one fact a lookalike name cannot fake.

AuthorizationRedirect.description: Where the consent page sends the browser next.

AuthorizationRequest.description: An authorization request, as the client put it in the authorize URL.

BulkDeleteIssues.description:
Bulk delete request: the listed `ids`, or every issue matching `filter`.
A body with neither or both matches no variant and is rejected, so an empty
body can never mean "all".

BulkUpdateIssues.description: Bulk mutate request: apply a status (and/or priority) to many issues.

CheckInResponse.description: One check-in, as the dashboard reads it.

CheckInStatus.description:
Status of one check-in. `Missed` and `Timeout` are only ever set by the
server.

ChunkUploadBody.description:
Multipart chunk upload.
Each part's **field name** may be the SHA-1 hex digest of that part's binary content
(sentry-cli v2 protocol, e.g. `da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709`) or an arbitrary
name like `file` (sentry-cli v3.x). Up to 64 parts per request; each part body is raw binary.

ChunkUploadOptions.description: Chunk upload capabilities, in sentry-cli's camelCase.

compression.description:
Required by the `sentry` npm uploader that Sentry SDK v11 bundler
plugins use; it rejects the response without it. Empty means chunks
are sent uncompressed, which is what `chunk_upload` reads.

CleanupCounts.description:
Rows affected by a cleanup, used symmetrically for the dry-run preview ("what
would be removed") and the executed result ("what was removed"). `spans` are
counted directly even though they cascade from `transactions`, so the UI can
show the true row impact. `issues_removed` is the number of issues that would
be left with zero events and therefore deleted.

source_maps.description: Unused source maps deleted; only a retention cleanup removes them.

CleanupFrequency.description: How often the cleanup that enforces retention runs.

CleanupKind.description: What the job is doing: deleting old data, or compacting the SQLite file.

CleanupRequest.description:
Request body for a cleanup (preview or execute): remove data older than
`older_than_days`, optionally scoped to a single project (omit for all).

`older_than_days` must be at least 1 — the service rejects smaller values,
since a window of 0 (or negative) would move the cutoff to now/the future and
purge the entire dataset.

include_events.description:
Whether to purge error events (and the issues they empty). Defaults to
`true` so an older client that omits it keeps the "delete everything"
behaviour.

include_logs.description: Whether to purge logs. Defaults to `true`.

include_transactions.description: Whether to purge transactions (and their cascaded spans). Defaults to `true`.

CleanupState.description: Where the instance's cleanup job is. There is at most one at a time.

CleanupStatus.description:
The cleanup job as the API reports it. Kept in memory: a restart forgets
it, and a run cut short by one is simply run again, since every batch it
committed is already gone.

error.description: Why a `failed` run stopped. Batches committed before it stay deleted.

removed.description: Rows removed so far while `running`; the total once it has finished.

CodeMapping.description: Maps a path as it appears in a stack trace to the path in the repository.

source_root.description: Prefix put in its place, e.g. `src/`. Empty for the repository root.

stack_root.description: Prefix stripped from the frame's path, e.g. `/app/` or `webpack:///./`.

CommentRequest.description: Body for creating an issue comment (note).

Compaction.description:
Whether the SQLite file can give the space a cleanup frees back to the
disk, and what compacting it once would take.

A database created before Rustrak set `auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` keeps
SQLite's default, `NONE`: its freed pages are reused but the file never
shrinks. One `VACUUM` rewrites it in incremental mode. Always
`needed: false` on Postgres, whose autovacuum gives the space back.

free_disk_bytes.description: Free disk next to the database, `null` when it cannot be read.

live_bytes.description: What the data in it takes, the part a compaction keeps.

reclaimable_bytes.description: Free pages inside the file, the part a compaction gives back.

required_disk_bytes.description:
Free disk a compaction needs: twice the live data, one copy in
SQLite's temporary file and one in the write-ahead log.

CreateAlertIntegration.description: DTO for creating an alert integration

CreateAlertRule.description: DTO for creating an alert rule

CreateAuthToken.description: DTO for creating a new token

body.description: Defaults to a summary with the culprit and a link back.

title.description: Defaults to the Rustrak issue's title.

role.description: Global role the invited user will receive (`admin` | `member`).

slug.description: Derived from `name` when left out. This is the slug SDKs check in with.

CreateProject.description: DTO for creating a new project

platform.description:
Platform identifier for the project, such as `python-django` or
`javascript-nextjs`. Rejected with a 400 if it is not one of the
supported values.

Optional. Omitting it is not the same as having no platform forever:
the project is then auto-assigned a platform from the first event it
ingests, drawn from the narrower set of platforms an event may declare.

DebugFileResponse.description: A debug information file as Sentry's `DebugFileSerializer` describes it.

DifAssembleFile.description: One file of a debug information file assemble request.

DifUploadBody.description: Multipart legacy debug file upload: one `file` part holding a zip.

fields.description:
Machine-readable annotations naming the inputs that were rejected.

Omitted from the JSON entirely when empty, so every consumer written
before this existed keeps seeing exactly the body it saw before.

incident_id.description:
Correlates this response with the `log::error!` line that carries the
detail [`INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE`] replaced.

Present on every 5xx and on nothing else: a 4xx says what went wrong in
`message`, logs nothing, and so has no line for an id to point at.

`nullable = false`: `skip_serializing_if` means the key is *absent* on
a 4xx, never `null`.

event_id.description: Sentry event ID: 32 hex digits, not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID.
Sentry event ID: 32 hex digits, not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID.

EventTimeseriesPoint.description:
One time-bucketed point in a project's error-event volume, split by severity.

`total` always equals `fatal + error + warning + info`: `info` absorbs
`debug` and any level the SDK sent that we do not model, so the stacked
segments of a chart always sum to the bar height and no events silently
vanish from the series.

FeedbackResponse.description:
A user feedback: its issue's state and what the user submitted
(`contexts.feedback`, develop.sentry.dev/sdk/telemetry/feedbacks/).

associated_event_id.description: The SDK id of the error event it is about.

attachments.description: Files sent with it, such as a screenshot.

url.description: The page it was sent from.

FieldError.description:
One rejected input, named as data rather than buried in the prose of
[`ErrorDetail::message`].

`field` is a **dot path into the request body** (`slug`,
`credentials.webhook_url`), not a JSON Pointer and not a UI label: a
consumer feeds it straight to a form library's `setError`.

The rejected *value* is deliberately never echoed back. One careless
application to a password input would put a credential in the log store.

The three fields are private on purpose. [`Self::new`] and [`Self::custom`]
are the only ways to build one, which is what makes "`message` is populated
only alongside [`FieldErrorCode::Custom`]" an invariant the compiler holds
rather than a convention a struct literal could quietly break.

message.description:
Only for what [`FieldErrorCode`] cannot express, and then only
alongside [`FieldErrorCode::Custom`]. Consumers pick their copy from
`(field, code)` so it can be translated, and never parse this.

`nullable = false`: `skip_serializing_if` means the key is *absent*,
never `null`, so a generated client must not model a null it can never
receive.

FieldErrorCode.description:
The closed vocabulary a [`FieldError`] may use.

Deliberately small and resource-agnostic: a large or per-endpoint
vocabulary becomes a public API that cannot be versioned. Adding a variant
is a wire change and requires the matching addition to the TypeScript union
in `packages/client/src/errors.ts`, which
`packages/client/tests/unit/app-error-contract.test.ts` enforces by parsing
this enum out of this file.

GenAiBreakdownRow.description: One row of a "top N by X" breakdown (model or tool name).

install_url.description: Where people install the app on an account or organization.

login.description: The person's GitHub username; `null` clears it.

GitHubRepository.description: A repository an installation can reach.

GitHubStatus.description: `GET /api/github`: everything the integrations page needs in one answer.

webhook_url.description: The address GitHub delivers webhooks to.

Grouping.description: Grouping model - maps a grouping key to an issue

InvitationInfoResponse.description: Public-facing invitation info for the accept page.

InvitationResponse.description: Public-facing invitation (no internal columns beyond what the UI needs).

IssueAggregates.description: Per-issue aggregates computed from recent events (capped scan).

IssueCategory.description:
Which kind of issue a list shows. Feedback is kept out of the default
list, as Sentry's `FeedbackGroup` is (`in_default_search=False`).

IssueGitHub.description: `GET .../issues/{id}/github`: the issue's "Code" block in one answer.

owners.description: Owners of the culprit file according to CODEOWNERS.

suspect_commits.description:
Commits that touched the issue's culprit file shortly before it first
appeared, newest first.

state.description: `open` or `closed`, as of the last webhook or sync.

is_resolved.description:
Deprecated: derived from `status`. Kept for the legacy client/UI until
they migrate to `status`. Remove in the client/frontend phases of #165.

trend.description:
24 hourly buckets, oldest to newest. Only populated by the issue list
endpoint.

user_count.description: Only populated by the issue list endpoint (bulk-computed per page).

user_report_count.description: Only populated by the single-issue GET endpoint.

IssueStatsWindow.description: How far back issue stats reach.

IssueStatusUpdate.description:
The status an update may set: an [`IssueStatus`], or `resolvedInNextRelease`
to resolve until the next release ships.

IssueTagValue.description:
A single tag value's usage within an issue — the shape `GET
/issues/{id}/tags/{key}` returns per entry, matching Sentry's
`TagValueSerializerResponse` (src/sentry/tagstore/types.py:166-173):
a bare list of these, not `{key, values}`.

name.description:
Display name for the tag key. Real Sentry has a reserved-key display
name table; Rustrak doesn't, so this currently just mirrors `key`.

IssueUpdate.description:
Body of an issue update: the fields of `GroupValidator`
(`api/helpers/group_index/validators/group.py`) Rustrak acts on.

KindAge.description: How long ago a kind of data arrived: rows per age bucket, and the oldest.

counts.description: One count per bucket, `AGE_BUCKET_DAYS.len() + 1` of them.

reference.description:
A GitHub issue or pull request URL, or `#123` for the project's
repository.

LogResponse.description: Response model for a single stored log in the list view.

severity_number.description: OTel severity number (1=trace … 21=fatal). None for unknown levels.

organization.description: Create the app under this organization instead of the user's account.

ManifestResponse.description: What the dashboard posts to GitHub to create the app.

McpSettings.description: Turns `/mcp` on or off: the body of `PUT /api/settings/mcp`.

McpStatus.description: Whether `/mcp` answers, and the URL to give an assistant.

url.description:
The configured endpoint (`PUBLIC_URL` + `/mcp`), which OAuth checks
the resource against; the browser's own origin may differ. `null`
without `PUBLIC_URL`, when signing in is off.

MetricDelta.description:
A counter measured over the requested window alongside the same counter
over the window immediately before it.

`previous` is `None` when the request asked for all time: there is no
earlier window to compare against, and reporting `0` there would render as
a misleading "+100%" in the UI.

MonitorConfig.description: A validated monitor configuration, with every default filled in.

MonitorConfigInput.description: `monitor_config` as an SDK or the dashboard sends it: every field optional.

MonitorEnvironmentResponse.description:
One environment of a monitor, with its most recent check-ins for the
timeline.

OAuthGrant.description: A connected client, as its user sees it.

OrgDetails.description: Synthetic organization sentry-cli checks before uploading.

timezone.description: IANA zone the schedule is read in. Defaults to UTC.

PreviewTemplateBody.description: Body of a template preview request.

transactions.description: Transactions; their spans are as old.

ProjectListStats.description:
The at-a-glance aggregates one row of the project-list table needs.

Deliberately narrower than [`ProjectStatsSummary`]: that one answers "how
is this project doing" for a page dedicated to a single project, this one
answers "which of my projects should I look at first" and must stay cheap
enough to compute for every project on the page at once.

events.description: Error events in the window, against the window before it.

new_issues.description:
Issues whose `first_seen` falls in the window, against the window
before it. Drives the "issues are climbing" signal, which event volume
cannot give: one noisy issue can multiply events without anything new
having broken.

open_issues.description: Issues currently unresolved, regardless of window.

trend.description:
Distinct issues that received at least one event in each bucket, oldest
first. Always `LIST_TREND_BUCKETS` long so the sparkline column renders
at a constant width whatever window was asked for.

Counts issues *active* in the bucket rather than issues *created* in
it. Creations are far too sparse to draw: a quiet self-hosted project
opens a handful of issues a day, which over 24 hourly buckets is three
lone bars in a field of zeros. Deliberately not summable — an issue
firing all day is counted in every bucket it appears in, so the series
is a shape, not a total.

ProjectMemberResponse.description: Member row joined with the user's email, for listing a project's team.

auto_create_issues.description: Open a GitHub issue for new issues that pass `auto_create_conditions`.

codeowners_rules.description:
How many ownership rules the last CODEOWNERS sync found; `None` before
the first sync.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: The project's own limits, or `null` when it follows the operator's.

rate_limited_event_count.description: Events the quota dropped after ingest had accepted them.

sentry_key.description:
The DSN's public key: its 32 hex digits in hyphenated UUID form
(8-4-4-4-12), not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID. The DSN carries the
same key without hyphens.

oneOf.description:
Present only when the request asked for `?stats_period=`.

Absent rather than zeroed when unrequested: a caller that did not ask
must be able to tell "no stats were computed" from "this project is
quiet", and only one of those should render an empty sparkline.

ProjectRetention.description:
A project that keeps its data for other windows than the defaults. Every
kind is set: an override replaces the defaults whole.

ProjectRole.description:
Per-project capability level for a member.

Ordered by privilege: `Viewer` < `Editor` < `Admin` (derived `Ord` uses
declaration order). An `Action` maps to the minimum role that may perform it.

ProjectStatsSummary.description:
Project-wide counters for the overview page, each with its previous-period
comparison.

events.description: Error events ingested in the window.

new_issues.description: Issues whose `first_seen` falls in the window.

open_issues.description: Issues currently unresolved, regardless of window.

period_hours.description: The resolved window in hours, or `None` for all time.

ProjectStorage.description:
Per-project storage breakdown, one row per project (including empty ones).

Counts are exact. `estimated_bytes` estimates the JSON payload length this
project holds across events, transactions, spans and logs: a sample of its
newest rows per table (spans, which have no ingest time, are sampled in no
particular order), scaled by the row count. It is exact for a project with
no more rows than the sample.

RateLimitsResponse.description:
Configure project routes
The server's per-project event limits (`MAX_EVENTS_PER_PROJECT_*`).

ReleaseHealthRow.description: Per-release health row returned by the stats endpoint.

next_run_at.description:
`null` while everything is kept forever, and for up to a minute after
the settings change.

RetentionRun.description: How the last retention cleanup went.

RetentionSettings.description:
Retention: how long each kind of data is kept, by default and per
project, and when the cleanup that enforces it runs. Stored as the
settings of the `storage_cleanup` scheduled job; a field left out takes
its default. Keeping everything forever runs nothing.

hour.description: Hour of the day it runs, UTC.

weekday.description: Day a weekly cleanup runs, 0 = Sunday.

RetentionWindows.description: How long each kind of data is kept, in days. `None` keeps it forever.

events_days.description: Error events, and the issues they leave empty.

oneOf.description: A five-field crontab, or an alias such as `@daily`.
Every `value` `unit`s, counted from the previous run.

SchedulePreview.description:
When a schedule runs next, computed by the code that runs it: monitors
expect their check-ins and scheduled jobs fire at exactly these instants.

SentryEvent.description:
Subset of `EventSerializer` for an error event
(`api/serializers/models/event.py`).

SentryIssue.description:
Subset of `GroupSerializer` plus its seen stats
(`api/serializers/models/group.py`), and `stats` when the caller asked
for a series (`StreamGroupSerializer`, `group_stream.py`).

annotations.description: Links to external issues; Rustrak keeps none, so always empty.

count.description: `str(times_seen)`: Sentry sends the count as a string.

id.description: The issue's `numeric_id`: Sentry's group ids are integers.

stats.description: `[unix_ts, count]` per bucket, keyed by stats period.

type.description: `error`, or `default` for an issue made of messages.

SentryProject.description:
Subset of `ProjectWithOrganizationSerializer`
(`api/serializers/models/project.py`). Sentry's ids are strings.

SentryRelease.description:
A release as `serialize_releases` (`api/helpers/group_index/index.py`)
falls back to it, with the serializer's `shortVersion`, which is the
version itself (`api/serializers/models/release.py`).

SentryStatus.description: `{"id", "name"}` of a status, as Sentry nests it in an organization.

SentryUserReport.description:
Body of a user report (`UserReportSerializer` in Sentry's
`api/serializers/models/userreport.py`), as the report was received.

eventID.description: The error event the report is about.

SentryUserReportRequest.description: Request body of a user report.

event_id.description: The error event the report is about.

SessionSummary.description: Project-wide session health summary, aggregated across all releases and environments.

SessionTimeseriesPoint.description:
One time-bucketed point in a project's session trend, aggregated across all
releases and environments. Powers trend charts (crash-free sessions over time).

SourceMapGcResult.description:
Outcome of a source-map garbage collection: orphaned `source_file` rows
(no `source_file_metadata` referencing them) removed from the DB and unlinked
from disk. `bytes_freed` is the exact summed `size` of the removed files.

SourceMapStorage.description:
Exact source-map storage weight, summed from the `size` columns.

Source maps live in two places: `chunk` holds the raw upload bytes as in-DB
BYTEA, `source_file` holds the assembled artifact on the filesystem CAS. Both
carry a `size` column, so the weight is an exact SUM — no filesystem walk.

chunk_bytes.description: Bytes held in the in-DB `chunk` table (raw upload chunks).

source_file_bytes.description: Bytes held on disk via `source_file` (assembled artifacts).

attributes.description:
The span's attribute bag, flattened to `{key: value}` regardless of
which producer wrote the row — see [`span_attributes`]. This is the
`gen_ai.*` payload (prompts, responses, tool arguments and results,
system instructions, tool definitions) that the agents UI renders.

tags.description:
Span tags, when the producer stored any. Spans Protocol v2 has no
separate tags concept — everything is an attribute — so this is always
`None` for a v2-origin span.

SpanDetailResponse.description:
One span with its full attribute bag — the detail counterpart to
[`SpanResponse`].

The list response deliberately omits attributes: `spans.data` is never
trimmed (unlike event data, which goes through `services::event_trim`), so
a single AI span can carry a whole prompt and a trace's worth of them would
dwarf the waterfall it is drawn from. Attributes are fetched one span at a
time instead, which is also how Sentry's own agent drawer works — the span
list is light and the details panel loads the selected node's attributes.

SpanResponse.description:
A single indexed span — extracted from a transaction, OR standalone
(Sentry "span" item type). Both origins write into the same `spans`
table, so `transaction_id` is the only thing that distinguishes them.

exclusive_time_ms.description: Relay's exclusive (self) time in milliseconds, if provided by the SDK.

gen_ai_operation_type.description:
gen_ai.* denormalized fields (story-ai-agent-monitoring.md, GH #180).
All `None` unless the span was recognized as an AI span.

platform.description:
Set for every span. A standalone span reports its own; a
transaction-embedded one is stamped with its parent transaction's at
write time, rather than being left NULL to be recovered by a JOIN —
the agents dashboard filters `spans` directly and a NULL would drop
the row from an environment-filtered view.

transaction_id.description:
The parent transaction, if this span was extracted from one.
`None` for a standalone span.

password_login_enabled.description:
Whether the login page should show the password form. False only when
the operator turned password sign-in off.

StorageAge.description:
The age of everything the instance holds, by project and kind, keyed on
ingest time like retention.

bucket_days.description: The buckets' upper bounds in days; the last bucket has none.

StorageSummary.description:
Instance-wide storage summary: what Rustrak is holding right now.

Row counts are exact (indexed `COUNT(*)`). `total_db_size_bytes` is a
best-effort figure from the backend (`pg_database_size` / SQLite page count),
while `source_maps` is exact (summed `size` columns).

TagSummary.description: A tag key with its most common values within an issue.

TagValueCount.description: A tag value with its event count within an issue.

TeamMemberResponse.description: A user as exposed on the team roster.

is_primary.description:
True for the first-registered (primary) account, which cannot be demoted
or deleted.

reason.description: Why nothing is sent, when `enabled` is false.

report.description:
The next heartbeat, exactly as it would leave. Shown even when
disabled, so the decision can be made on the real thing.

sink.description: Where it goes, when `enabled` is true.

response_body.description: What the endpoint answered, when it answered anything.

TestIntegrationBody.description: Request body for the test-integration endpoint.

ToggleRequest.description: Body for toggling a per-user flag (bookmark/subscription).

TransactionDetailResponse.description:
Response model for a single transaction detail view.

Carries the same summary fields as [`TransactionResponse`] plus the full
Sentry payload under `data` (spans, contexts.trace, measurements, tags,
request, user). The frontend builds the span waterfall and metrics view
from `data`.

data.description: Full Sentry transaction payload (spans, contexts, measurements, tags, request, user).

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds (timestamp - start_timestamp). None if start_timestamp is missing.

event_id.description: Sentry event ID: 32 hex digits, not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID.

TransactionResponse.description: Response model for a single transaction in the list view

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds (timestamp - start_timestamp). None if start_timestamp is missing.

event_id.description: Sentry event ID: 32 hex digits, not necessarily an RFC 4122 UUID.

TransactionStatsResponse.description:
Aggregate performance stats for one (transaction_name, op) group.
Powers the performance overview: throughput + latency percentiles +
failure rate per transaction. Percentiles are continuous (linear
interpolation, matching Postgres `percentile_cont`).

count.description: Number of transactions in this group.

failure_rate.description: Fraction (0.0–1.0) of transactions whose trace status is set and not "ok".

UpdateAlertIntegration.description: DTO for updating an alert integration

UpdateAlertRule.description: DTO for updating an alert rule

UpdateIssueState.description:
Request to update issue state.

`status`/`substatus`/`priority`/assignment are the canonical fields.
`is_resolved`/`is_muted` are accepted as a deprecated compatibility shim
and mapped onto `status`.

assigned_to.description:
`None` when omitted, `Some(None)` when the client sent an explicit
`null` (clears the assignment), `Some(Some(id))` to assign.

UpdateMonitor.description:
Body of `PUT /api/projects/{project_id}/monitors/{slug}`. Fields left out
keep their value, including each field of `config`.

UpdatePreferencesRequest.description:
What a reader may change about how the dashboard is presented to them.

Every field is doubly optional, and both levels are used: absent means
"leave it", `null` means "clear it". `#[serde(default)]` with
`deserialize_with` is what keeps those distinguishable, because plain
`Option<Option<T>>` collapses a missing key and an explicit null.

platform.description:
Manual override of the project's platform, such as `python-django` or
`javascript-nextjs`. Rejected with a 400 if it is not one of the
supported values.

The supported set is wider than the platforms an event may declare, so
framework-specific identifiers are accepted here. An update overwrites
any auto-assigned value, which is how a wrong detection is corrected.
Sending `null` leaves the current value untouched rather than clearing
it.

rate_limit_per_hour.description: The same for the hour, against `MAX_EVENTS_PER_PROJECT_PER_HOUR`.

rate_limit_per_minute.description:
The project's own events-per-minute limit. It can only tighten the
operator's `MAX_EVENTS_PER_PROJECT_PER_MINUTE`, never raise it.
Absent leaves it as it is; `null` removes it.

slug.description:
New slug, slugified before storing.

A slug already taken by another project returns a 409. It is not
silently de-duplicated the way a slug derived at creation time is,
since storing something other than what was requested would be wrong.

Sending `null` leaves the current value untouched.

auto_create_conditions.description:
The same filters an alert rule takes: `min_level`, `environments`,
`min_events`.

UpdateRelease.description:
DTO for `PUT .../releases/{version}/` — generic partial update.
Setting `date_released` IS "finalize": there is no separate status flag.
Absent fields (including an explicit `null`) leave the stored value
unchanged, matching Sentry's own partial-update semantics for this endpoint.

UpdateUserRole.description: Request body for changing a user's global role.

UserReport.description: A user feedback report attached to a project/issue/event.

UserReportRequest.description: Body for submitting user feedback on an issue.

is_admin.description: Convenience flag derived from `role` (kept for backward compatibility).

language.description: Chosen dashboard language, or `null` when the user never chose one.

timezone.description: Chosen IANA timezone, or `null` when the user never chose one.

UserRole.description:
Instance-wide role for a user.

`Admin` has full access to every project and to team management.
`Member` only sees projects they are a member of (see `ProjectRole`).
